bibliographic.title: Enhancing Efficiency of Pension Schemes through Effective Risk Governance: A Kenyan Perspective
bibliographic.citation_apa: Namagwa, S. W. (2025). Enhancing efficiency of pension schemes through effective risk governance: A Kenyan perspective. Journal of Financial Risk Management, 14(3), 304–324. https://doi.org/10.4236/jfrm.2025.143017

methodology.method_family: quantitative panel data analysis with mediation testing
methodology.study_design: panel data study examining mediating effect of risk management
methodology.sample_description: 896 observations from 128 pension schemes in Kenya over 2015–2021
methodology.sector: pension funds / retirement benefits / financial services
methodology.technology_context: corporate governance and financial risk management in pension schemes; no LLM, generative AI, or conversational systems mentioned

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study examines corporate governance, risk management mediation, and efficiency of Kenyan pension schemes using panel data. The provided text contains no LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or AI governance mechanisms relevant to the review scope.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper addresses governance, risk management, and compliance in a regulated financial domain (pensions), it is entirely about board-level corporate governance and pension scheme efficiency. It does not study conversational AI, LLM-based systems, or generative AI governance. Generic governance and risk terminology in a pre-AI financial context does not meet inclusion criteria for a systematic review on conversational governance in LLM systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Absence of LLM, generative AI, and conversational system content is unambiguous in the provided abstract and introduction excerpts.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on limited front-matter text only. Methodological detail on estimation, variables, and robustness checks is not available in the provided excerpts. Study appears internally coherent for its stated pension governance question but is off-topic for the LLM conversational governance review.

cerqual.explanation: For the target review on LLM conversational governance, relevance is effectively nil. Limited excerpt prevents full methodological assessment; available text shows a clear empirical objective and defined sample but insufficient detail on analysis procedures.

coding.theme: Corporate and risk governance in pension schemes
coding.subtheme: Mediation of risk management between governance structures and scheme efficiency

synthesis.main_claim: Risk management significantly mediates the relationship between employee representatives on the board of trustees (as a component of corporate governance) and the efficiency of pension schemes in Kenya.
synthesis.contribution: Empirical evidence that strong risk management practices enable governance structures—particularly employee board representation—to contribute to improved pension scheme efficiency and sustainability.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text notes potential sampling bias against firms of different dispositions; broader methodological limitations not fully visible in excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from evidence synthesis. Not usable for claims about LLM, conversational AI, or generative AI governance. At most, distant analogical context for governance-in-regulated-finance, which is outside the defined review scope.
